plates.caption_as_written: My diplomatic reading (uncertain points in brackets): 'Ægirz hialmur h[ann] sk[al] / giorast á blý og þrycka / [í] enni sier [þann?] á von á / óvin sinum að h[ann] mæti / h[onu]m og muntu hann yfirvinna / (h[ann] er so f[...] h[...] ept[ir] [...])'. Paraphrase (mine): 'Ægir's helm: it shall be made in lead and pressed on the forehead [of one] who expects to meet his enemy, and you will overcome him.' The last, bracketed line is not legible to me. Note the spelling Ægirz/Ægirs-, not Ægis-.
plates.form_as_seen: Small central circle; eight straight arms at roughly 45 degrees cross at the centre inside the circle. Every arm carries THREE short crossbars about half-way out and ends in a CURVED fork: an arc set across the arm, its horns pointing outward, with the shaft running up to it (a crescent-trident). No ring-ends. Freehand, so arms and arcs are not exactly equal, but all eight arms are of the same type. The arm-ends are curved, not the straight-pronged tridents of modern reproductions.

Lbs 143 8vo (1030x1710 px, parchment, sooty) is legible; the figure is clear, the caption mostly readable, its last line not. AM 434 a 12mo (1812x2593 px) figures are clear but tiny (each c. 300-430 px); captions are abbreviated 15th-c. script I did not transcribe. Lbs 4627 8vo fol. 14v is faint pencil. Lbs 2413 8vo (c. 1011x1350 px) is legible but low resolution (figures 60-120 px each on fol. 31v).

findings: Shelfmarks: the Huld manuscript is ÍB 383 4to (handrit.is), not Lbs 143 8vo; Lbs 143 8vo is the parchment Galdrakver dated 1670 (cert. medium). The task text's 'Huld manuscript (Lbs 143 8vo, 1847)' conflates them.

Huld date: handrit.is gives 1860 (cert. medium). Fol. 1r carries the note 'Frá Geir Vigfússyni á Akureyri 1874' (provenance). On p. 5 (fol. 3r) the scribe writes 'Annus Christi' in Greek acrophonic numerals and glosses it '1869'. Neither 1847 nor 1860 was seen on the leaves viewed; 1869 may be the year that page was written (not proof for the whole book).

Huld vegvísir locator: p. 60 is fol. 26v (handrit.is label 0026v; '60' written top left), not fol. 27r. Fol. 27r is the next page (No. XXX Herðslustafir, unnumbered) and 27v is blank. The 'one account' giving 26v is right by the repository's foliation.

Huld vegvísir caption as written: 'Beri madur stafi þessa á sér villist madur ekki í' (right, downward) / 'hridum né vondu vedri þó ókunnugur sé.—' (left, upward). This confirms the plural 'stafi þessa' and the ending 'sé', not 'sá'.
Huld vegvísir form: the eight arms meet at a POINT, with no central circle and no enclosing ring. The research's 'small central circle' does not fit Huld, Lbs 2917 a or Lbs 4627.

Huld numbers its staves I–XXX (pp. 51–60 and fol. 27r). The vegvísir is No. XXVII, which confirms '30 staves'. The numbering of pages 41–50 is absent (fol. 21 is blank or ruled), so page and folio numbers do not run in step.

Huld names no ægishjálmur, Gapaldur, Ginfaxi, Smjörhnútur or Hulinhjálmur among Nos. I–XXX. The eight-armed figure of the helm type there is No. XXI 'Salomons Insigli' (p. 58, 'Berist á sér til varnar').

Þjófastafur in Huld covers different kinds of thing: No. XVII (a framed figure with diagonals), No. XVIII (a curved figure with an eye), Nos. XIX and XX (ROWS of 13 and about 20 cipher-like signs, not one figure) and No. XXVIII (eight-armed, p. 60). The headings differ in number: Nos. XVII, XVIII and XXVIII read 'Þjófastafur' (singular), Nos. XIX and XX 'Þjófastafir' (plural).

Lbs 143 8vo: the eight-armed helm is on fol. 11r (folio '11' written; label 0011r), so Crazy Alchemist's locator is right and Gelmir's 10v is not; 10v holds an alphabet and small staves. The caption spells it 'Ægirz hialmur' and says to make it in lead and press it on the forehead before meeting an enemy.
Lbs 143 8vo helm form: a central circle, eight arms each with THREE crossbars, and each arm ending in a CURVED crescent-fork. These are not the straight-pronged tridents of modern reproductions.

AM 434 a 12mo is in Copenhagen (Den Arnamagnæanske Samling, per handrit.is), dated s. XV² (1490–1510, after Kålund's Katalog). It already has EIGHT-armed staves on fol. 4vb (forked ends) and fol. 5ra (ring-ends), besides four-armed ones (5rb, 5vb); handrit.is calls the staves on ff. 4vb–5vb 'variations of Ægishjálmur'. So 'the eight-armed form first appears in Lbs 143 8vo' holds only for a figure NAMED ægishjálmur. The captions were not transcribed and the name was not read on these leaves.

Wrestling pair: in Lbs 2413 8vo, fol. 20v, the names are 'Ginfaxi' and 'Gapandi', not Gapaldur. The caption reads 'Ginfaxi á hæl, Gapandi á tá, taktu á sem fyrri, því nú liggur á', which puts Ginfaxi on the HEEL and Gapandi on the TOE. That is the reverse of the research's placement (Gapaldur under the heel, Ginfaxi under the toes). No right or left foot is named.

Lbs 2917 a 4to (Olgeir Geirsson, 1868–69) uses one name for different figures. No. 99 'Ginnir (1)' (p. 60), No. 113 'Ginfaxi (2)' (p. 69) and No. 121 'Ginfaxi (3)' (p. 73) are three unlike figures numbered as one series, and the register (fol. 5r) lists No. 121 as 'Ginnir (3)'. Angurgapi (1) is No. 100 (p. 61) and Angurgapi (2) No. 114 (p. 69). No 'Gapaldur' appears in the register (Nos. 1–124).

Lbs 2917 a 4to vegvísir: No. 27 on p. 27 (fol. 15r), titled „Vegvísir“, with the caption 'beri maður þennan staf á sér mun maður trauðla [runes] í [runes] …'. This confirms Vlasatý's p. 27. Its figure follows the Huld figure closely.

Lbs 4627 8vo vegvísir: fol. 17v, 'Að maður villist ekki. Geym þennan staf undir þinni vinstri hendi, hann heitir „Vegvísir“', with Christian lines ('Guð gefi mér lukku og blessun í Jesú nafni …'). The instruction is to keep it under the LEFT hand. The figure follows the Huld scheme with different details, so 'visibly different' is true of the details only.

Lbs 2413 8vo, fol. 31v, confirms from the manuscript the 'nine helms': 'Þetta eru þeir níu Ægirs Hjálmar sem enginn má án vera … og skal hvör 99 brúkaður vera', followed by nine different small figures. The manuscript spells the name Ægirs-, as Lbs 143 8vo does.

Lbs 2917 a 4to No. 83 'Ægirshjálmur fagri (hinn gamli)' (p. 51; so spelled on the page, 'Ægishjalmur (fagri)' in the register) is a circle-enclosed figure used to see a thief in one's sleep. No. 119 'Ægishjálmur (2)' (p. 72) is the tine-and-crossbar type closest to the modern standard, but without a central circle.

Dates and contents from the handrit.is TEI records: Lbs 2413 8vo is c. 1800 (1780–1820), 74 leaves, one hand. Lbs 4627 8vo is 19th century (cert. low), 32 leaves, three hands, from Eyjafjörður. Lbs 2917 a 4to is Olgeir Geirsson, 1868–1869, 58 leaves.
The TEI records of the Landsbókasafn manuscripts carry <availability status='restricted'>: 'Aðgangur aðeins mögulegur í fræðilegum tilgangi'. No image licence was found.

corrections.was: 'Á sama máta má líka, til að vita hvor frá manni stelur, rista seinasta (næsta) staf á mannlaugarbotn utan og innan, með fullu [tungli] og flóði; en sumir rita hann á blýplötu ... leggja síðan undir höfuð sér, og mun þig þjófinn dreyma; les pater noster' (partly normalised; my reading).
corrections.now: 'Á sama máta má líka, til að vita hvor frá manni stelur [written over, darker ink], rista seinasta (næsta) staf á munnlaugarbotn, utan og innan, með fullu [drawn moon face] og flóði; en sumir rita hann á blýplötu, með nýjum stálknífi, á sunnudag um miðdag, leggja síðan undir höfuð sér, og mun þig þjófinn dreyma; les pater noster' (spelling normalised a little; my reading).
